items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Well she would tell me to watch Fats.

ctx.x: Did he continue playing after that? Right. Played until he died.

Well he had his own little group and his wife was the pianist in the band. Never had any great musicians. It was him and her. That was the biggest part of the band. And then they would just pick up any musicians. Fats and Lady Yes got to be a real contrary fellow. Couldn't anybody get along with him. I imagine that's because he was getting sick. And a man gets in a place where he's sick all the time. He becomes irritable and can't get along with anyone. He had this disease, the Bryce disease. But I stayed with…

He'd go there every night when Juanita would go off to play at this club. He'd go there and sit on the outside to keep Fats company. And Fats was on the last thing. Because he needed to see him alone.
